phrases.notes: الْحِوَار (al-ḥiwār = the dialogue) + الأَوَّل (al-awwal = the first). Adding 'Al-' strips away the tanween (double vowel).
Standard Islamic greeting. Combining 'Al-' with a word removes the tanween.
Standard response. The damma on 'alaykumu' facilitates smooth vocal transition into 'as-Salām'.
إِسْم (name) + ـِي (my Yā' of ownership/belonging). Khalid takes tanween as a standard masculine proper noun.
مَا (what) + اسْمُكَ (your name). The attachment of the masculine possessive suffix -ka indicates address to a male.
إِسْمِي (my name). Khalil ends with tanween damma.
كَيْفَ (how) + حَالُكَ (your state/condition). The suffix -ka targets a male listener.
The standalone masculine pronoun أَنْتَ ('you') is added at the end for explicit emphasis ('And how are YOU?').
